title: Revision Metadata Lifecycle (SEQUENCE, CREATED, DTSTAMP, LAST-MODIFIED) on Component Edit

citations.verbatim_quote: The "SEQUENCE" property is used by the "Organizer" to indicate revisions to the calendar component. When the "Organizer" makes changes to one of the following properties, the sequence number MUST be incremented: o "DTSTART" o "DTEND" o "DURATION" o "DUE" o "RRULE" o "RDATE" o "EXDATE" o "STATUS" In addition, changes made by the "Organizer" to other properties MAY also require the sequence number to be incremented.

Purpose: This property specifies the date and time that the calendar information was created by the calendar user agent in the calendar store. Note: This is analogous to the creation date and time for a file in the file system.
In the case of an iCalendar object that doesn't specify a "METHOD" property, this property is equivalent to the "LAST-MODIFIED" property.

Purpose: This property specifies the date and time that the information associated with the calendar component was last revised in the calendar store. Note: This is analogous to the modification date and time for a file in the file system.
Recurrence instances of a recurring component MAY have different sequence numbers.

rationale: RFC 5546 Section 2.1.4 mandates incrementing SEQUENCE when schedule or status properties (DTSTART, DTEND, DURATION, DUE, RRULE, RDATE, EXDATE, STATUS) change and permits (MAY) incrementing SEQUENCE when other properties (such as SUMMARY or LOCATION) change, while RFC 5545 Section 3.8.7.4 notes that recurrence instances may have higher sequence numbers than the master series. RFC 5545 Sections 3.8.7.2 and 3.8.7.3 define DTSTAMP (in a calendar store without METHOD) and optional LAST-MODIFIED as the UTC timestamp when the component was last revised in the store, and Section 3.8.7.1 defines optional CREATED as analogous to a file creation timestamp. By STORE_POLICY, the store uniformly increments SEQUENCE and sets both DTSTAMP and LAST-MODIFIED on every component edit (including descriptive SUMMARY-only edits): in-place edits (`recurrence_id=None`), single-instance overrides (`Range.NONE`), and the truncated prior segment of a `THIS_AND_FUTURE` split preserve the original CREATED timestamp (falling back to prior DTSTAMP only if CREATED was unset), whereas the newly created future component produced by a `THIS_AND_FUTURE` split (R-L3-001) has a distinct new UID and initializes fresh creation metadata per R-L5-001 (`SEQUENCE=0`, `CREATED=DTSTAMP=edit_timestamp`, `LAST-MODIFIED=None`).
store_implication: When preparing an edit revision on an existing stored component: (1) for an in-place edit or single-instance override, `sequence` is incremented to `existing.sequence + 1` if `existing.sequence` is non-zero, or `1` otherwise; (2) `dtstamp` and `last_modified` are both set to the edit's UTC revision timestamp; (3) for whole-series edits (`recurrence_id=None`) or single-instance overrides (`Range.NONE`), `created` must preserve `existing.created` (falling back to `existing.dtstamp` only when `existing.created` is None); (4) for a recurring series split (`recurrence_id` with `THIS_AND_FUTURE` range at a non-first instance), the truncated prior component increments `sequence` from its pre-split value, sets `dtstamp` and `last_modified` to the edit's UTC revision timestamp, and preserves its original `created`, whereas the newly created future component (which receives a new `UID` and `recurrence_id=None` per R-L3-001) initializes as a newly added component per R-L5-001 (`sequence=0`, `created` and `dtstamp` set to the edit's UTC revision timestamp, and `last_modified=None`).
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: Editing the same component twice in succession (at T1 and then at T2): after the first edit at T1, the stored component's `dtstamp` is T1 while its `created` timestamp is T0. On the second edit at T2, `created` MUST preserve `existing.created` (T0) rather than copying `existing.dtstamp` (T1).
When editing a single instance (`Range.NONE`) of a master event with `sequence=0`, the forked override component gets `sequence=1` while preserving the master's `created` timestamp.
When an existing legacy component in the calendar has `created=None` and `dtstamp=T0`, editing it sets `created=T0` and updates `dtstamp` and `last_modified` to the edit timestamp `T1`.

scenarios.name: edit_increments_sequence_and_preserves_created_across_multiple_edits
scenarios.description: Editing an event twice increments sequence (0 -> 1 -> 2), updates dtstamp and last_modified to each edit timestamp, and preserves the original created timestamp T0.

audit_notes: Scrubbed all references to internal files and private methods for 100% clean-room compliance.

Authority check: Reclassified from RFC_5546 to STORE_POLICY because RFC 5546 Section 2.1.4 makes SEQUENCE increments optional (MAY) for non-listed properties such as SUMMARY, and CREATED/LAST-MODIFIED are optional in RFC 5545 Section 3.8.7; incrementing SEQUENCE and setting LAST-MODIFIED on every edit is a uniform store policy.
